text:
New Jersey arrives with a bruise. The Devils' four-game winning streak ended in a 5-2 loss at Colorado two days ago, but they're still 4-1-0 in their last five and close a three-game road trip tonight. Vegas snapped a three-game winless run with a 4-1 win over Ottawa, where Raphael Lavoie scored his first NHL goal. The Golden Knights are without Parker Wotherspoon, and Brayden McNabb plays his 900th NHL game.

The teams look close in our numbers: we have it at 3.03 expected goals for New Jersey and 2.95 for Vegas. At five on five, the Devils have taken 58% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Vegas 55%. New Jersey is better than its record, with a +5 goal difference against +13.1 expected, but finishing and goaltending have cost them. Both power plays create about the same, while Vegas kills penalties better, allowing 0.38 expected goals per game to New Jersey's 0.47. In net, projected starter Connor Hellebuyck is +0.71 in goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots would suggest) in one start, and projected Vegas starter Carter Hart is -0.73. Last season Hellebuyck was +3.43 over 57 games and Hart -4.44 over 18.

Jack Hughes is our top pick for New Jersey at a 34% chance to score and 70% to get a point. As The Athletic's Jesse Granger posted, he lost teeth again against Dallas. Mitch Marner brings an eight-game point streak (1 goal, 10 assists) at 64% to get a point. Mark Stone leads Vegas at 34% to score, though we think he's due to cool.
